153.s: He and Pearl adopted Dee Dee and Tony; after 39 years he met Francine on a Duke Ellington cruise and describes her.
153.ch: Ellington years, Pearl Bailey and Jazz at the Philharmonic
153.q: We found out that she couldn’t have children, so we adopted two kids: Dee Dee, when she was four months old, and Tony, who just passed away a couple of months ago. My son. 51 years old. He got real sick. Dee Dee – that’s [a picture of] Dee Dee up in the corner there – she’s about 42 now. A good…

153.t: Pearl's earlier marriages and her Georgetown doctorate
153.s: He explains her family nickname Aunt Dick, her earlier unhappy marriages, and her achievements including a Georgetown degree earned over seven years.
153.ch: Arranging, bandleading and Pearl Bailey's life
153.q: Yeah. It didn’t work out. One was an alcoholic. Another was into drugs. So when we finally got together, the family was happy that somebody was taking care of Pearl. Because they wanted another boy, before she was born. That’s why they called her Aunt Dick. They didn’t call her Pearlie. The…

689.t: Lizzie Miles as a school friend, and her husband Pajot
689.s: Dominique went to school with Lizzie Landry (Lizzie Miles), brought her to Chicago, and recalls her husband and meeting her again.
689.q: I went to school with Lizzie Miles. Her name was Lizzie Landry. Her and I was in the same room. And I hope when you go to New Orleans, tell them you saw Dominic Dillacone play that went to Mary Lee's school with you.

251.t: Wedding anniversary, daughter's wedding and the children
251.s: Albert describes the double anniversary with his daughter Lynette's wedding, renewing vows at Corpus Christi, and son Kenneth's marriage.
251.q: Yes, it was the 46th anniversary of being married to Hazel, and our daughter was married the same day, so now we have a double anniversary on the 8th of September. Well, it's been 46 beautiful years. Like everything else, it's had its ups and downs. We've had some lean days, we've had some fat…

257.s: Asked about early bands he heard, he mentions his wife's family, the Bijou name, and her mother's musical relatives.
257.ch: Neighborhood halls and the Ida Cox tour
257.q: that she came from here. Could have been, but the relation of hers is on her mother's side. Yeah. I've been with Johnny Dave. This fellow used to play Sight's iPhone. I can't think of him now. Oh, it's a gob of him. Well, anyhow, they used to rehearse along Calderest Street. Yeah. Well, I used to…

632.s: Reminiscence about Lawrence Marrero's family and the custom of a married wife and an outside wife.
632.ch: Noon Johnson and other local figures

404.t: Photographs of Mitchell and his wife
404.q: But they didn't take that picture right though. You see I had on a yellow planter shirt and my hat, that straw hat was a bluish color. You know what I mean? Well they never colored it.

370.t: Life in the nightclub world at the Blue Angel
370.s: After marrying Max she lived among the Blue Angel crowd and raised two daughters, mixing up Alfred and Max.
370.ch: Marriage, Max Gordon and leaving Alfred
370.q: married, and we eventually had two daughters, and we eventually went on to live a very different life than I had lived with Alfred in music. Now I was in the nightclub world. Alfred had another club on East 55th Street...

373.s: Daughters from the first two marriages and sons from his present marriage; his wives' backgrounds and how he met them.
373.ch: Civil liberties, family and the press
373.q: Yeah. I’m the only person who’s been married three times and the last one will reach it’s fiftieth year, I think, next year. That’s part of the surprises of longevity, I guess. The first wife I got to know [as] part of a jazz circle in Boston. Her parents had been supporters of Sacco and Vanzetti.…

103.t: Second marriage to Lorraine; becoming father and grandfather the same day
103.s: He discusses marrying Lorraine, their daughter Barbara, being a father and grandfather at once at the Embers, and his eight grandchildren.
103.ch: The rhythm section, family and records
103.q: Oh, Milt, you forgot something. Milt, you know I was sitting in the Embers nightclub and I was sitting with my wife and my daughter and both of them was pregnant and do you know, I became a father and a grandfather at the same time!
